title: TheStradman's Wrecked Ferrari 812 Superfast Nears the Finish After Nearly Three Years
dek: The ex-Michael B. Jordan 812 he bought for $187,000 on eBay is "98% done" in Porsche grey, and the frame damage made the bill much larger than planned.

source.where: eBay Buy It Now listing from a Sacramento shop that had bought the car after the insurer sold it as a total loss in early 2024
source.boughtNote: Stated by TheStradman in his first video, as reported by autoevolution [3][4]; the eBay asking price was $198,999.
source.title: unknown
source.damage: Front passenger-side impact with a parked car: right front wheel torn off, fender and mirror missing, windshield and passenger window broken, headlight cracked, three airbags deployed, seatbelts unusable, right-side suspension suspect; aluminum frame twisted with a baseball-size hole; dented oil tank.

episodes.t: My Crashed Ferrari is 98% Done. The Ultimate Transformation.
episodes.what: TheStradman shows the crashed Ferrari close to complete after its custom transformation; the title gives no model, and we treat it as the 812 Superfast, the channel's only crashed-Ferrari project.

parts.part: Paint in Porsche Paint to Sample Geyser Grey Metallic (Fix Auto Provo)

time: About two years and eight months: bought around late March 2024, frame damage found in April 2024, engine out by September 2024, painted in Utah before September 2026, and "98% done" on November 13, 2026. No shop hours given.

costs.note: Counts the stated $187,000 purchase and five priced parts: bumper $9,809, fender $5,761, windshield $3,788 and oil tank $2,200 as stated, plus $10,000 for carbon-ceramic rotors, his own estimate. Frame repair, airbags, seatbelts, paint, any body kit, transport and labor have no published price and are not counted, so the real total is higher.

value.basis: Clean 812 Superfasts sold for $425,000 to $478,000 on Bring a Trailer in late 2026, and a dealer asked $459,900 for a 2021 in January 2026; we take about $460,000 as clean value. Sports Car Market's appraiser source puts salvage-title discounts at 30% to 50%, with structural damage at the deep end, which gives roughly $230,000 to $320,000. The custom color narrows the market and the celebrity and YouTube history may offset some of that; title status unconfirmed.

comps.what: 2021 Ferrari 812 Superfast, about 6,900 miles (asking price, Ferrari South Bay)

verdict: Probably not a money-maker, and it was never really priced to be one. TheStradman paid $187,000 for a wreck with a twisted frame, and known parts already push the stake past $218,000 before frame work, airbags, paint or labor [3][4]. A clean 812 Superfast now sells for $425,000 to $478,000 [11], but a structurally repaired, recolored car on a likely branded title could lose 30% to 50% of that [13]. That leaves a resale range near what he has likely spent in all. The return is in the videos: nearly three years of content from one wreck.
body:
## The buy

TheStradman, the YouTube channel run by James Condon, has spent most of the last three years rebuilding the Ferrari 812 Superfast that actor Michael B. Jordan crashed in Hollywood in December 2023 [3][5]. When the wreck first came up for sale in January 2024, autoevolution described it as a 2021 812 Superfast in powder blue over a dark red interior, offered as-is with no reserve, with a pre-accident valuation of $567,001 [2]. The insurer had written it off [3].

The 812 did not go straight from the insurer to Condon. According to autoevolution's account of his first video, a Sacramento shop bought it roughly a month after the crash, then relisted it on eBay about two months later with a $198,999 Buy It Now price [3]. Condon paid $187,000 and trucked it out of Sacramento, and he bought it without seeing it in person [3][4]. He suspected the shop had found a problem that made it sell again quickly, and that suspicion proved right.

## The damage

The car had slid into a parked Kia Niro, taking the hit on the front passenger corner [2][3]. Condon's own list ran long: the right front wheel torn off and later refitted, a missing front fender, a broken windshield, a shattered passenger window, a cracked right headlight, a missing passenger mirror, three deployed airbags, unusable seatbelts and a suspect right-side suspension [3][4].

The expensive surprise came once the panels were off. In the April 2024 frame video [6], he found the aluminum frame twisted from the impact, with "a hole the size of a baseball in it" (autoevolution's paraphrase of the video) [4]. Carscoops reported him saying the budget "has been completely destroyed" [5]. Months later, pulling the engine took more than four days, and Supercar Blondie reported that the team admitted the job was far more than they expected [7][8].

## The work and the parts

The parts Condon priced on camera in 2024 are the only itemized costs on record. From Ferrari he quoted a new front bumper at $9,809 and a passenger-side fender at $5,761 [4][5]. A new windshield was $3,788, and he put a pair of carbon-ceramic front rotors at about $10,000, his own estimate rather than an invoice [4]. A dented oil tank came to $2,200 [7]. The airbags, seatbelts, frame straightening and paint were never given a price in the coverage we could find.

The car did not go back to stock. In "My Crashed Ferrari 812 Superfast is Reborn" [9], the shell was prepared and painted at Fix Auto Provo in Utah in Porsche Paint to Sample Geyser Grey Metallic rather than a Ferrari color, according to WheelCircuit's write-up of that episode [10]. The latest episode, posted November 13, 2026, is titled "My Crashed Ferrari is 98% Done. The Ultimate Transformation." [1]. Its title does not name the model, and the description is a sponsor read, but the 812 is the only crashed Ferrari the channel has been rebuilding, so this file treats it as the same car.

## The money

Counting only what has been stated, the 812 has cost at least $218,558: the $187,000 purchase plus $31,558 in priced parts. That is a floor. The frame repair, the airbags and belts, the custom paint and any body kit are all missing, as is labor. On a car with structural damage those items could plausibly double the parts figure, but no number has been published, so we do not add one.

Against that, clean cars have climbed. Bring a Trailer sold a 2018 812 Superfast with 14,000 miles for $478,000 in October 2026 and a 2019 with 20,000 miles for $425,000 in September 2026 [11]. In January 2026 a Ferrari dealer was asking $459,900 for a 2021 with under 7,000 miles [14]. Two years earlier, in March 2024, a 3,700-mile 2018 had sold on Bring a Trailer for $330,000 [12].

This car will never be priced like those. An insurer total loss normally leaves a branded title, though the coverage never says what title Condon's car carries. Appraiser Dave Kinney told Sports Car Market that the usual 30% salvage discount understates it: "I've seen 50%" [13]. Structural damage, as here, pushes toward the bigger cut. A non-factory color narrows the buyer pool further, while the celebrity history and the YouTube build might widen it for a certain kind of buyer.

## What's next

At 98% done, the remaining work is presumably finishing and shakedown, and the next episode should be a reveal or first drive. Condon has not said whether he will keep or sell it. The open questions for the record are the total he has spent, what title the car wears, and whether Ferrari dealers will service a car with this history.
